chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most evil of the people on the Day of Judgment will be those who are honoured out of fear of their evil.'

key_terms.اتِّقَاءَ شَرِّهِمْ: Out of fear of their evil/harm

ai.seo_question: Who are the most evil people on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* critiques the social phenomenon of *ittiqā’ al-sharr* (fearing one's evil), where status is derived from the avoidance of harm rather than moral excellence. It serves as a profound ethical warning against superficial honor based on fear rather than genuine merit, highlighting that such individuals will be the worst on the Day of Judgment.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir Bin Abdullah having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most evil of the people on the Day of Judgment will be those who were being honoured (in the world) out of fear of their evil’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu Hamza from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
The most evil among people on the Day of Judgment will be one whom people respect for fear of his evil manners’”
